question.text: How do declared category shares vary across samples and facets?
question.population_or_system: the sampled units represented in composition.csv

claims.statement: The figure describes category shares under each sample's declared denominator.
claims.scope: samples with a complete declared category grid
claims.not_claimed: Differences are statistically significant or causal.

primary: sample-level category counts converted to shares

panels.question: What fraction of each sample belongs to each category?
panels.quantity_and_units: share of the declared within-sample count denominator (0–1)

encoding.position: sample on x, within-sample share on y
encoding.color: one stable color per declared category
encoding.order: declared facet, sample, and category orders

panels.unique_contribution: preserves each sample while making the common denominator explicit

data_integrity.missingness: missing category rows are not permitted; known zeros must be explicit

transformations.operation: divide each category count by its positive within-sample total
transformations.guard: all values finite and nonnegative; complete category grid; denominator greater than zero

data_integrity.aggregation: input is preaggregated to one row per facet, sample, and category

limitations: relative composition does not show absolute totals

visual_system.emphasis: sample-level composition under a common denominator

color_semantics.category: stable across every sample and facet

review_risks.risk: composition bars hide differences in absolute totals
review_risks.mitigation: limit the claim to relative shares and report totals elsewhere when scientifically relevant

acceptance: every included input row appears once in analysis-table.csv
all sample shares close to one without silent renormalization
SVG, PDF, and PNG match the declared physical size and PNG DPI
the final SVG has editable text and no clipping
